subject: Catalyst Analytics — marketplace onboarding & private-offer checklist
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ashok Rao <ashok@catalyst-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Catalyst Analytics — marketplace onboarding & private-offer checklist

Hi Ashok,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great discussion on the latency/cost targets for your dosing predictions workload. Per our conversation, I attached a draft mutual action plan (MAP) that organizes the remaining procurement and onboarding steps so we can close via an AWS Private Offer. The high-level asks in the MAP are:

- Confirm procurement contact and preferred PO flow (direct invoice vs. marketplace private offer).
- Vendor setup requirements (tax forms, W-9 / VAT as needed).
- Legal checklist: approved terms vs. redlines (SLA, data residency, indemnity).
- Billing mapping: which AWS account will accept the private offer, and whether billing should be routed to their master payer.
- Evaluation cadence: 2-week controlled eval with predefined promtsets and success metrics (latency P95 < 220ms, token cost target < $0.003/token).

Quick ask: can your procurement contact review the attached MAP worksheet and return with the preferred PO path and any internal timing constraints? If private offer is the route, please include the AWS account ID that will accept the offer.

Proposed timeline (we can accelerate if needed):
- Mar 10: Share MAP + procurement checklist (today).
- Mar 12: Procurement confirms PO path and account ID.
- Mar 15: Issuance of draft PO / acceptance of private offer.
- Mar 17–24: Onboarding + test run on dedicated capacity / private offer acceptance.

I’m copying Ben (pricing lead) and Karthik (partner ops) to help with the offer details and marketplace flows.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v2.xlsx

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0148
From: Ashok Rao <ashok@catalyst-analytics.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@catalyst-analytics.com>, procurement@catalyst-analytics.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Catalyst Analytics — marketplace onboarding & private-offer checklist

Lauren,

Appreciate the clear MAP — very helpful. I’ve looped Priya (procurement lead) and our procurement inbox here. A few notes from our side after a quick internal sync:

- We prefer the AWS Private Offer route to keep billing on our consolidated payer.
- Our procurement timeline is tight: we need purchase paperwork in hand by Mar 15 to meet quarter-close on Mar 31.
- I attached our internal procurement timeline (high-level) which shows an internal PO approval path and the expected legal review window.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you confirm the exact marketplace flow if we accept a private offer (what the acceptance link will look like and whether Redwood needs AWS Marketplace seller action)?
2) Do you have a sample PO language we can attach to our approval packet (pricing line, contract term, renewal cadence, support SLA)?

We’ll aim to confirm the account ID by EOD Mar 12. If we can keep the paperwork lightweight and use the private-offer acceptance + a short purchase order, we can probably hit Mar 15.

Thanks,
Ashok

--
Ashok Rao
Director, AI Platforms

ashok@catalyst-analytics.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Catalyst Analytics — marketplace onboarding & private-offer checklist

Lauren / team,

Quick pricing & billing notes to include in the packet:

- Pricing: Standard committed monthly for Dedicated capacity with overage billed at usage rates; for private offer we can provide a mapped SKU with a unit price (see MAP tab 'Pricing lines').
- Marketplace flow: Redwood will create the AWS Private Offer and send Catalyst the accept link. Once they accept, their account ID is recorded and AWS issues billing to the mapped account. Redwood needs the account ID beforehand to configure the offer.
- Invoice cadence: billing will flow through AWS Marketplace invoices for the private offer; Redwood will also provide a consolidated usage statement for reconciliation per month.

I attached a short sample PO blurb to copy into their internal packet (one-line price/term + support contact + Redwood tax info). Also flagged legal to prepare a short SOW if they want a bespoke term set — otherwise we can proceed on standard terms + PO.

Attachments: Catalyst_Procurement_Timeline.pdf

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
